==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|unic|unick||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
Borrowed from {{bor|en|fr|unique}}, from {{der|en|la|unicus}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/juːˈniːk/|/jəˈ-/<a:weak vowel>}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-unique.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|iːk|s=2}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj|er,more}}

# {{senseid|en|one of a kind}} {{lb|en|uncomparable}} Being the only one of its [[kind]]; [[unequaled]], [[unparalleled]] or [[unmatched]].
#: {{syn|en|one of a kind|sui generis|singular|one-off}}
#: {{ux|en|Every person has a '''unique''' life, therefore every person has a '''unique''' journey.}}
#* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=3|passage=‘{{...}} There's every Staffordshire crime-piece ever made in this cabinet, and that's '''unique'''. The Van Hoyer Museum in New York hasn't that very rare second version of Maria Marten's Red Barn over there, nor the little Frederick George Manning—he was the criminal Dickens saw hanged on the roof of the gaol in Horsemonger Lane, by the way—’}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1998
|author=Paul M. Edwards
|title=The Korean War: An Annotated Bibliography
|url=https://archive.org/details/koreanwarannotat0000edwa/
|publisher=w:Greenwood Press
|ISBN=0-313-30317-7
|LCCN=97-40189
|OCLC=477058097
|page=114
|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/koreanwarannotat0000edwa/page/114/
|text=A very interesting history of United Nations at war in Korea, done in an{{sic}} '''unique''' question and answer style.}}
# Of a feature, such that only one holder has it.
# [[particular|Particular]], [[characteristic]].
#* {{quote-book|en|title=Problems '''Unique''' to the Holocaust|author=Harry J. Cargas|year=1999|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=yvI7UWVNWSwC&printsec=frontcover#v=onepage&q&f=false|footer=[see the book title]}}
# {{senseid|en|rare or unusual}} {{lb|en|often|{{glossary|proscribed}}}} [[rare|Rare]] or [[unusual]].
#* {{quote-book|en|passage=And as I look back, it seems to me that we were '''fairly unique''', the sixty of us, in that there wasn’t one good mixer in the bunch.
|title=For Esmé—With Love and Squalor
|author=J.D. Salinger
|year=1950}}

====Usage notes====
* The comparative and superlative forms ''uniquer'' or ''more unique'' and ''uniquest'' or ''most unique'', as well as the use of ''unique'' with modifiers as in ''fairly unique'' and ''very unique'', are criticised with the reasoning that either something is unique or it is not. These modified senses of “unique”, however, have been in use since at least as far back as the 18th century, with “unique” taking its common secondary sense of “uncommon, unusual, remarkable”.
